lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The adjective suffix -less
The key word motionless ends in the suffix -less. Words ending in -less are usually
adjectives. Adjectives describe people, places, and things. Examples: helpless babies,
cloudless skies, useless junk. When the suffix -less is added to a word, the meaning of
the word changes.

might learn more.” In these sentences, less is a word, not a suffix.

same as the word in bold-faced type).
1. seeing numerous animals
a. wild b. lost c. sick d. many
2. the motor in the fan
a. air b. heat c. machine d. blades
3. a motel near the highway
a. car b. sign c. picnic d. building
4. as motionless as a statue
a. still b. hard c. carved d. beautiful

exercises.title: EXERCISE B
lines: Meaning in Context
Use these words to fill in the blanks in the following paragraph.
numerators motive numerical motivate
Eddie has always loved numbers. When he first learned to count,
he painted numbers on his toy cars. Then he lined them up in
(1) order from one to five. Now he enjoys learning
about fractions and working with (2) and denomina-
tors. Eddie's (3) for always doing his math homework
first is simple enjoyment. Perhaps his love of numbers will later
(4) him to become a mathematician or an accountant.

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The adjective suffix -less
The key word motionless ends in the suffix -less. Words ending in -less are usually
adjectives. Adjectives describe people, places, and things. Examples: helpless babies,
cloudless skies, useless junk. When the suffix -less is added to a word, the meaning of
the word changes.
Less can also stand alone. Then, it is a word meaning “fewer; a smaller amount.”
You can say, “After dogs shed, they have less hair,” or “If you would talk less, you
might learn more.” In these sentences, less is a word, not a suffix.
Make new words by adding the suffix -less to each of these words. Write the new
word on the line.
1. care
2. worth
3. fear
4. thought
5. sleep
6. Look at the five words you wrote. What meaning does the suffix -less have in
these words? Circle your answer.
A. without B. full of C. against
7. Write a sentence using the adjective motionless.

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The noun suffix -ness
The key word studiousness ends in the suffix -ness. Studiousness is a noun. You know
that many nouns name persons, places, and things. But nouns can also name
qualities (like softness and kindness) and conditions (like sickness and tardiness). Note
that all the preceding names for qualities and conditions are nouns that end in the
suffix -ness.
The underlined nouns in the questions below name qualities. Look at the pictures.
Then answer the questions.
A. B. C.
1. Which picture makes you think of darkness? Circle your answer. A B C
2. Which picture makes you think of playfulness? Circle your answer. A B C
3. Which picture makes you think of brightness? Circle your answer. A B C
Now, take away the suffix -ness from each underlined noun above.
4. Write the three words that would be left.
5. Which part of speech is each of the three words you wrote? Circle your answer.
A. noun B. verb C. adjective
6. When you add the suffix -ness to an adjective, what part of speech is the word
you make? Circle your answer.
A. noun B. verb C. adjective
7. Write a sentence using the noun studiousness.

The key word various is an adjective. Adjectives describe nouns. Many words that
end in -ous are adjectives that describe nouns. Examples: famous explorers, spacious
fields, vigorous exercise.
Make new words by adding the suffix -ous to each of the words that follow. Write
the new words on the line.
1. joy
2. courage
3. danger
4. Which adjective that you wrote best describes firefighters?
5. Which adjective that you wrote best describes a very happy person?
6. Which adjective that you wrote best describes boating without a life jacket?
7. Which meaning best fits the suffix -ous? Circle your answer.
A. not having B. having C. against
8. Write a sentence using the adjective various.

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary

The key word specify ends in the suffix -fy. Specify is a verb. You know that some
verbs like run, jump, and swim show physical action. Verbs can also show other
kinds of action. Examples: notify (to tell, to make known), falsify (to change so as
to make false), fortify (to make stronger or more secure).
The underlined verbs in the questions below express three kinds of action. Look
at the pictures. Then answer the questions.
A. B. C.

2. Which picture makes you think of the verb beautify? Circle your answer. A B C
3. Which picture makes you think of the verb solidify? Circle your answer. A B C
Match the verbs that end in -fy/-ify with their definitions.
4. satisfy A. to make clear
5. clarify B. to make united
6. unify C. to make satisfied

A. to fix B. to fill C. to make
8. Write a sentence using the verb specify.

root_meaning: species meaning “a particular type or kind”
definition: A group of plants or animals that share common features.
example: The rain forest is home to hundreds of different species of frogs. The English word species and the Latin word species are exactly the same. Some people call these words from different languages that look similar and come from the same root “cognates.” It is interesting to note that the word species has remained exactly the same for over two thousand years.

example: In class, we say "specification" when we talk about special kinds or types.

exercises.title: Using ROOT CLUES
lines: The roots famil (closely known) and speci (particular kind) give you clues
about meaning. When you spot one of these roots in a word, you have a key
to the word's meaning. Use the underlined root clues to help you match the
following columns:
l. familiar A. a person with a particular kind of knowledge
2. specialist B. well known and close
3. familiarize C. to point out a particular kind
4. specify D. to get to know
The root clues did not give you complete definitions as the following dictionary
listings will. But they got you started by giving you part of the meaning.
Sometimes that part helps you to figure out the word.

exercises.title: EXERCISE A
lines: Synonyms
Write the letter of the best SYNONYM (the word with the meaning most nearly the
same as the word in bold-faced type).
1. to familiarize the class with
a. supply b. attend c. leave d. acquaint
2. visited a specialist in coins
a. writer b. expert c. speaker d. beginner
3. a comfortable familiarity
a. closeness b. friend c. distance d. blanket
4. specifying the medicine he wanted
a. picturing b. remembering c. naming d. forgetting

exercises.title: EXERCISE B
lines: Meaning in Context
Use these words to fill in the blanks in the following paragraph.
specific familiar specialty species
Along the river, Agnes spotted a brown bird with a black beak that she
thought she had seen before. It looked very (1) . But
she was not sure what (2) it was. Birds were her
(3) , so Agnes liked to identify each one she saw. She
hunted through her bird guide, which gave (4)
information about a variety of birds living in her state. When she found a
picture of the brown bird, she quickly learned its name.

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The verb suffix -fy/-ify
The key word specify ends in the suffix -fy. Specify is a verb. You know that some
verbs like run, jump, and swim show physical action. Verbs can also show other
kinds of action. Examples: notify (to tell, to make known), falsify (to change so as
to make false), fortify (to make stronger or more secure).
The underlined verbs in the questions below express three kinds of action. Look
at the pictures. Then answer the questions.
A. B. C.
1. Which picture makes you think of the verb terrify? Circle your answer. A B C
2. Which picture makes you think of the verb beautify? Circle your answer. A B C
3. Which picture makes you think of the verb solidify? Circle your answer. A B C
Match the verbs that end in -fy/-ify with their definitions.
4. satisfy A. to make clear
5. clarify B. to make united
6. unify C. to make satisfied
7. Circle the meaning that best fits the verb suffix -fy/-ify.
A. to fix B. to fill C. to make
8. Write a sentence using the verb specify.

definition: Active describes something connected to taking action and getting things done.
example: The word active helps me describe things that are about taking action and getting things done.

exercises.title: Using ROOT CLUES
lines: The roots act (act) and offic (work) give you clues about meaning. When you
spot one of these roots in a word, you have a key to the word's meaning. Use
the underlined root clues to help you match the following columns:
l. officer A. to work as a referee or umpire
2. officiate B. to act on making an idea into a law
3. actor C. a person who works to keep others safe
4. enact D. a person who acts in movies
The root clues did not give you complete definitions as the following dictionary

Sometimes that part helps you to figure out the word.

exercises.title: EXERCISE A
lines: Synonyms
Write the letter of the best SYNONYM (the word with the meaning most nearly the
same as the word in bold-faced type).
1. the officials for the game
a. players b. teams c. referees d. cheerleaders
2. actually found a way
a. gradually b. quietly c. fearfully d. really
3. the actor at the front of the stage
a. performer b. director c. teacher d. writer
4. to enact into law
a. read b. make c. choose d. familiarize

exercises.title: EXERCISE B
lines: Meaning in Context
Use these words to fill in the blanks in the following paragraph.
activity officer officiate active
Elections were coming up for offices in the Chess Club. Tess thought she
would like to become an (1) , maybe even president.
She had been an (2) member of the club for over a
year. Playing chess was her favorite after-school (3) .
Since she had watched the president (4) at club
meetings and chess tournaments, Tess was sure she could do the job. But
could she get enough votes to be elected?

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The adjective suffix -ive
The key word active is an adjective. It ends in the suffix -ive. This suffix tells
you that someone or something is doing the action. An active person describes
someone who acts or participates.
Look at how other adjectives that end in -ive are related to their roots.
The adjective cooperative describes someone who cooperates.
The adjective creative describes someone who creates, invents, or has original ideas.
The adjective talkative describes someone who talks a lot.
Make new words by adding the suffix -ive to the following words. Write each new
word on the line.
1. attract
2. support
3. impress
4. invent
5. possess
6. Look back at the five words you wrote. Could they be used to describe people?
Circle your answer.
A. yes B. no
7. Write sentences using two of the words you wrote.

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The verb suffix -ate
When the suffix -ate is added to a noun like captive, it forms a verb, captivate. Look
at how the nouns office and motive become verbs when -ate is added to them—
officiate and motivate.
But be careful when you see the letters of this suffix. They may not be a suffix. The
past tense of eat is ate, and this is a complete word. Example: He ate a sandwich. In
addition, the letters a, t, and e form a very common ending to many familiar one-
syllable words, such as gate, late, mate, skate, hate. In these words the letters a, t, and
e have no special meaning.

a suffix.
educate plate create rotate punctuate
decorate crate fate date navigate
Words in which -ate is a suffix

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The noun suffix -tude
The key word gratitude ends in the suffix -tude. Gratitude is a noun. So are most
other words that end in the suffix -tude. Examples: attitude, solitude, fortitude.
From finding locations on a map, you probably know two more words that end in
-tude. They are longitude and latitude. The lines of longitude run north and south.
The lines of latitude run east and west. The measurements of longitude and
latitude help people describe exact locations.
Words that end in the suffix -tude can also tell about height and size. Examples:
altitude (how high), multitude (how many), magnitude (how large).
Look at the pictures. Then fill in the lines below.
A. B. C.
1. Write the letter of the picture that makes you think of the word latitude.
2. Write the letter of the picture that makes you think of the word altitude.
3. Write the letter of the picture that makes you think of the word
longitude.
4. Write a sentence using the noun gratitude.

you spot one of these roots in a word, you have a key to the word's meaning.
Use the underlined root clues to help you match the following columns:
l. classify A. not thankful
2. classic B. thanks
3. ungrateful C. a book that is part of a group of lasting stories
4. gratitude D. to put into groups
The root clues did not give you complete definitions as the following dictionary
listings will. But they got you started by giving you part of the meaning.
Sometimes that part helps you to figure out the word.

exercises.title: EXERCISE A
lines: Synonyms
Write the letter of the best SYNONYM (the word with the meaning most nearly the
same as the word in bold-faced type).
1. a generous gratuity
a. graduate b. thought c. person d. tip
2. acting in an ungrateful way
a. unfriendly b. uneasy c. useful d. unappreciative
3. a word with a classical root
a. Latin b. Swiss c. Chinese d. Indian
4. to gratify his desire for a pet dog
a. notice b. satisfy c. build d. specify

exercises.title: EXERCISE B
lines: Meaning in Context
Use these words to fill in the blanks in the following paragraph.
classification gratitude classic classify
Sierra said to Zach, “Charlotte's Web was good to the last page. That book
deserves to be called a (1) .”
Zach looked up from his science homework and asked, “How would you
(2) the spider Charlotte? Is she an insect?”
“No,” said Sierra. “That (3) isn't correct. A spider is
an arachnid, not an insect.”
“Thanks,” said Zach, with a smile of (4) . “That is the
last bit of information I needed for my science homework.”

exercises.title: EXERCISE C
lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The noun suffix -tude
The key word gratitude ends in the suffix -tude. Gratitude is a noun. So are most
other words that end in the suffix -tude. Examples: attitude, solitude, fortitude.
From finding locations on a map, you probably know two more words that end in
-tude. They are longitude and latitude. The lines of longitude run north and south.
The lines of latitude run east and west. The measurements of longitude and
latitude help people describe exact locations.
Words that end in the suffix -tude can also tell about height and size. Examples:
altitude (how high), multitude (how many), magnitude (how large).
Look at the pictures. Then fill in the lines below.
A. B. C.
1. Write the letter of the picture that makes you think of the word latitude.
2. Write the letter of the picture that makes you think of the word altitude.
3. Write the letter of the picture that makes you think of the word
longitude.
4. Write a sentence using the noun gratitude.

definition: Gratefully tells us that something happens in a way related to showing thanks and appreciation.
example: It reminds me that something happens in a way that connects to showing thanks and appreciation.

lines: Extend Your Vocabulary
The noun suffix -tude
The key word gratitude ends in the suffix -tude. Gratitude is a noun. So are most
other words that end in the suffix -tude. Examples: attitude, solitude, fortitude.
From finding locations on a map, you probably know two more words that end in
-tude. They are longitude and latitude. The lines of longitude run north and south.
The lines of latitude run east and west. The measurements of longitude and
latitude help people describe exact locations.
Words that end in the suffix -tude can also tell about height and size. Examples:
altitude (how high), multitude (how many), magnitude (how large).
